items.stem: A box of mass 3 kg rests on a horizontal floor and a vertical force of 12 N pushes down on it. List the forces acting on the box and state the direction of each.
items.answer: weight 30 N down; applied force 12 N down; normal reaction 42 N up
items.markingKey: B1 all forces; B1 directions and values [2]

items.stem: A box of mass 20 kg rests on a horizontal floor and is pulled upwards by a vertical string with tension 10 N, but does not leave the floor. Daniel says the normal contact force is 200 N because it always equals the weight. Explain the error and find the correct value.
items.answer: R balances all the other vertical forces, not just the weight: R = 200 − 10 = 190 N.
items.markingKey: B1 R depends on all vertical forces; B1 correct value [2]

items.stem: A box of mass 3 kg rests on a horizontal floor and a vertical force of 8 N pushes down on it. Draw a force diagram and find the normal contact force on the box.

items.stem: A box of mass 2 kg rests on a horizontal floor and is pulled upwards by a vertical string with tension 5 N, but does not leave the floor. (a) Find the normal contact force exerted by the floor on the box. (b) State the force exerted by the box on the floor, giving its direction. (c) State the mass of the box and its weight.
items.answer: (a) 15 N (b) 15 N downwards (Newton's third law) (c) 2 kg; 20 N
items.markingKey: (a) M1 resolves; A1 value [2] (b) B1 value and direction [1] (c) B1 [1]

items.stem: A car of mass 1200 kg moves along a straight horizontal road. The driving force is 3000 N and the resistance to motion is 500 N. Find the acceleration.
items.markingKey: Resultant force = ma.

items.stem: A car of mass 1200 kg moves along a straight horizontal road. The driving force is 1500 N and the resistance to motion is 300 N. Arjun says that the acceleration would be the same if the mass were doubled. Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: a = F/m, so doubling the mass (with the same resultant force) halves the acceleration to 0.5 m s⁻².
items.markingKey: B1 a = F/m; B1 halves [2]

items.stem: A load of mass 5 kg is raised vertically by a rope with tension 52.5 N. Grace says that the acceleration would be the same if the mass were doubled. Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: a = F/m, so doubling the mass (with the same resultant force) halves the acceleration to 0.25 m s⁻².
items.markingKey: B1 a = F/m; B1 halves [2]

items.stem: A particle of mass 5 kg is pulled along a smooth horizontal surface by a horizontal force of 12 N. Tariq says that the acceleration would be the same if the mass were doubled. Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: a = F/m, so doubling the mass (with the same resultant force) halves the acceleration to 1.2 m s⁻².
items.markingKey: B1 a = F/m; B1 halves [2]

(b) Find the distance travelled while braking to rest.

items.stem: A car of mass 1000 kg moves along a straight horizontal road. The driving force is 2400 N and the resistance to motion is 900 N. It starts from rest. After 5 s the driving force is removed and the brakes apply an additional force of 4000 N; the resistance is unchanged. (a) Find the acceleration of the car while the driving force acts. (b) Find the speed after 5 s. (c) Find the deceleration while braking.
items.answer: (a) 1.5 m s⁻² (b) 7.5 m s⁻¹ (c) 4.9 m s⁻²
items.markingKey: (a) M1 D − R = ma; A1 a [2] (b) B1 value [1] (c) M1 includes both resistance and braking force; A1 deceleration [2]

items.stem: A person of mass 50 kg stands in a lift that is accelerating downwards at 0.5 m s⁻². Find the normal contact force on the person.
A person of mass 75 kg is in a lift accelerating upwards at 2 m s⁻². Tomás finds the normal force to be 600 N. Explain the error and correct it.
items.answer: The resultant force must be in the direction of the acceleration (upwards): R = m(g + a) = 900 N.
items.markingKey: B1 direction of resultant; B1 correct R [2]
